body:
Hi! Try to put your `else` block into an `` block as it shown in the [changelog](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#enhanced-ngif-syntax) Like this: ```

{{login}}

User had been removed: {{user.removed | date : 'dd.MM.yyyy'}}

User is active

 ```
Please add a plunker that reproduce the issue. Without further details we will close the issue. Thanks.
The problem is because you are using `removed : null` when `{{null}}` is printed in HTML it throws that error. Check this [plunker](https://embed.plnkr.co/Uz15BY53QrOOTrysLbD5/)

@1heg0d exactly, then you be set to a template ref: `<ng-template #activeBlock>User is active</ng-template>` solves your issue.

I'll leave this open so that we improve the error message.

rename.to: ngIf cryptic error when a then block is set to a non template

body: The conclusion is you CAN'T use ngIf then else without ng-template ? o.O

@titusfx In short, yes. The *ngIf directive is a structural directive with the asterisk character * being a syntatic sugar, and it expects you to pass `` for the else condition's `TemplateRef` in the [ngIf directive code](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ec56760c9ba530ee98117f9dd451b43c28d6de67/packages/common/src/directives/ng_if.ts#L148) to grab the referenced markup correctly. When you write `
Test
`, it really becomes this: ```
Test
 ``` And when you write this: ```
Test
Else template
 ``` For more info, read these sections: https://angular.io/guide/structural-directives#what-are-structural-directives and https://angular.io/guide/structural-directives#the-asterisk--prefix.
